videos.hook_text: Flip a coin 10 times in a row -- what are the odds you get ALL heads?
videos.notes: First ledger entry for this slug -- no prior analytics to retrieve, so bet is pure variety: every segment gets its own new mechanic (narrowing gates, dice tower, shrinking card fan, growth line) instead of repeating the bar/bubble kit defaults that were previously on 2 of 4 segments.

timeline.detail: coin flip curiosity question over narrowing-odds-gates build-in
dice-probability-tower: sum-7 tower rises tall vs matching short 2/12 towers
shrinking-deck-fan: card fan loses a card, target card glows, odds tick up
growth-line-photo: seedling rides the rising application-index line
closing line: luck was math nobody calculated

videos.hook_text: Somewhere right now, a language is taking its last breath -- and it happens every 14 days.
videos.notes: Fixed a real data bug while authoring: language_distribution's Mandarin point was 1.3 (should be 1300, i.e. 1.3 billion) which made the top language render as the smallest bar -- corrected the unit and added the missing Hindi/Arabic points so the say line's 5-language claim actually matches the data. Kept exactly one photo+number layout (the flag ground-row) per house variety rule; the other 3 segments are fresh procedural mechanics.

timeline.detail: a language dies every 14 days, over urgency-dials build-in
flag ground-row: Mandarin/Spanish/English/Hindi/Arabic sized by native speakers
digital-silence-globe: globe lit only 10% up, dark zone dotted with fading languages
seedling-revival-meter: revival dial + sprouting leaves for the 15%/yr learner growth
closing line: half of today's 7,000 languages could go silent

videos.hook_text: The air itself is changing, and we have the receipt.
videos.notes: Kept the existing trend/pictograph split (already good variety); rewrote the closing from a flat summary into an escalation using the decadal-acceleration numbers (1960s +8.77ppm vs 2010s +24.11ppm, ~3x) so the last beat implies the 2020s will beat it, not just restate the topic.

timeline.detail: CO2 line trend build-in over the receipt hook
2010s tripled the 1960s pace, 2020s already on track to beat it

videos.hook_text: Two countries hold more than a third of all humanity.
videos.notes: Existing pictorial_race + waffle_grid split already varies well; swapped the closing from a flat 'wild, right?' summary into a concrete personal-consequence line (1 in 3 people you meet) using the 35.3% combined China+India share already on screen.

timeline.detail: every 3rd person you meet is Chinese or Indian

videos.hook_text: Guess which single fuel still out-generates solar and wind combined, worldwide.
videos.notes: Rewrote the hook from a flat statement ('here's how the planet made its electricity') into a guess-the-answer curiosity gap using coal's 34.4% vs wind+solar's combined 15% -- info-first hooks under-hold per doctrine, question hooks should test better on this format.

timeline.detail: fossil fuels dropped under 60% for the first time since the 1940s

videos.hook_text: Malaria dropped for two decades straight -- then last year it shot right back up to sixty four per thousand people at risk.
videos.notes: All 3 segments were identical object-ground-row photo layouts -- a hard VARIETY violation (at most one photo+number layout per video). Kept the internet-growth segment as the one photo row, invented a new mosquito-swarm-tide mechanic for the headline malaria stat (swarm SIZE falls then regrows with the data, matching the title's twist), and switched the open-defecation segment to fill_object so no two segments share a layout.

timeline.detail: mosquito-swarm-tide: swarm shrinks 2000-2018 then regrows to 2024
world got more connected and sanitary, but old diseases came back

videos.hook_text: We fenced off more ocean and land than ever before -- and still hauled out more fish than any year in history.
videos.notes: Segment 1 had NO scene at all (hard validation failure) -- invented a new cropland-tiles mechanic (a land grid fills with real farmland photos as % of land climbs) to fix it and give the story its own signature mechanic. Simplified the protected-area segment to a single centered fill_object so it no longer duplicates the timeline_axis+stack structure of the fish-catch segment.

timeline.detail: fill_object globe: protected area up to 17.0%
farms, catches, and protected zones all grew at once

videos.hook_text: One slice of the world's energy pie sat frozen for thirty years -- then it exploded. Guess what changed.
videos.notes: All 3 segments were identical 5-photo-object ground rows (worst VARIETY violation in the batch: same structure, only the subject photo changed). Moved the renewable-energy segment to the named 'trend' chart, kept the headline alternative+nuclear segment as the photo row, and invented a new bulb-chain mechanic for electricity access (lit-bulb COUNT out of 20 IS the % electrified). Also rewrote the hook from a flat stat-reveal into a guess-what-changed curiosity gap.

timeline.detail: bulb-chain: electricity access bulbs light up to 91.9%
energy is changing faster than the headlines admit

videos.hook_text: Everyone assumes cities are exploding faster than ever -- but urban growth just hit its slowest pace in over fifty years.
videos.notes: Segments 1 and 3 both used the object-ground-row layout (2 of 3 photo+number layouts violates the at-most-one rule). Switched the rural-growth segment to 'stack' (house-icon COUNT crashing from ~8 to ~2 depicts the 1.64%->0.3% collapse better than two static houses anyway), leaving object/fill_object/stack as three distinct types across the video.

timeline.detail: the world is aging fast and spreading out slower than ever

videos.hook_text: Landlines just fell to a number we haven't seen since before some of you were born.
videos.notes: Segments 1 and 3 both used the object layout (landline photos vs cell-phone ranking photos) -- switched the mobile-subscriptions ranking to the named 'pictorial_race' chart (a natural fit for a country ranking) so the video carries object/stack/classic-chart instead of two photo rows. Sharpened the hook with a generational-memory angle; kept the strong wire-in-the-wall closing.

timeline.detail: object rows: landlines 1972/2004/2025 rise then fall
the wire in the wall lost, the wire in your router won
